name: Learning from all beings (the avadhūta's method)
method_summary: Observing the ways of the elements, animals and people and drawing from each a lesson for detachment and knowledge, as the avadhūta took twenty-four teachers and his own body as a twenty-fifth.

name: Bee-like alms (mādhukarī)
method_summary: The renunciant takes a little food from many houses without burdening any and stores nothing for later.

name: The python's way (ājagara-vṛtti)
method_summary: Living without striving for food or comfort, accepting whatever comes and remaining still if nothing comes.

warnings.text: The Bhāgavata frames this for the sage who has given up striving; the text does not prescribe a fast but acceptance of what comes (U06 note).

name: Living alone (ekacaryā)
method_summary: The sage wanders alone, homeless and unobtrusive, because many people cause quarrel and even two cause talk.

name: Holy company (satsaṅga)
method_summary: Seeking out and serving the holy, hearing the talks that arise in their company; the Yoga Vāsiṣṭha's fourth gatekeeper, the Bhāgavata's means that wins the Lord, the first of the Adhyātma Rāmāyaṇa's nine means.
signs_of_progress: faith, attraction and devotion arise in order (Kapila Gītā 3.25.25)

name: Meditation on the Lord in the heart-lotus (Uddhava Gītā)
method_summary: Seated evenly with gaze at the nose-tip, after breath purification with Oṃ, visualize the eight-petalled heart-lotus with sun, moon and fire in its pericarp and the four-armed Lord in the fire; meditate on each limb, then on the smiling face, then fix the mind in space and finally think of nothing, seeing the self in the Lord as light in light.
signs_of_progress: the delusion of object, knowledge and act ceases (11.14.46)

name: Breath purification with Oṃ (Uddhava Gītā)
method_summary: Purifying the breath's path by inhalation, retention and exhalation and their reverse, raising the unbroken Oṃ from the heart like a bell's sound; the text gives it as done ten times at each of the three junctions of the day, mastering the breath within a month.

name: Concentrations yielding the siddhis (Uddhava Gītā)
method_summary: Kṛṣṇa describes, for each of the eighteen powers, a concentration of the mind on a particular aspect of the Lord; summarized here without the individual procedures.

warnings.text: The siddhis are obstacles and a waste of time for one practising the highest yoga; the goal of yoga is not reached by them.

name: Image worship (kriyā-yoga, Uddhava Gītā)
method_summary: Worship of the Lord in Vedic, tantric or mixed mode, in an image (of stone, wood, metal, paste, painting, sand, mind or jewel), on prepared ground, in fire, sun, water or the heart; with love even water suffices.

warnings.text: Worship in images while despising the Lord present in all beings is 'offering into ashes'.

name: Seeing the Lord in all beings and bowing to all
method_summary: Regarding every being as the Lord, with equal vision toward brāhmaṇa and outcaste, prostrating even to dog, outcaste, cow and donkey, ignoring others' laughter, until the vision of the Lord in all arises; images are worshipped only until the Lord is known in one's own heart and in all beings.

name: The twelve yamas and twelve niyamas (Uddhava Gītā)
method_summary: Practising the twelve restraints and twelve observances listed in 11.19.33-35.

name: Kapila's eight-limbed yoga with meditation on the Lord's form
method_summary: Duty, contentment, service of self-knowers, moderate pure food, solitude, the yamas and niyamas, posture, gradual mastery of breath, withdrawal, holding breath in one of its seats with the mind, meditation on the Lord's form limb by limb, and samādhi.
signs_of_progress: melting heart, hair standing on end, the mind attaining nirvāṇa like a flame (3.28.34-35)

name: Attributeless devotion
method_summary: Letting the mind flow to the Lord at the mere hearing of his qualities, without motive or interruption, desiring nothing, not even liberation, apart from his service.

name: Inquiry (vicāra) as the Yoga Vāsiṣṭha teaches
method_summary: Reflecting, with scripture and the wise, on 'who am I? what is this world?', discriminating the Self from body, senses and mind until the seen is known not to exist apart from consciousness; Cūḍālā's daily self-questioning is the model.

equivalents.note: related to the later practice of self-inquiry (recent teachers); not asserted identical

name: Practice of Brahman (brahmābhyāsa)
method_summary: Thinking of Brahman, speaking of it, awakening one another to it and being wholly devoted to it; spending nights in reflection on the teaching of the Self.

name: Cultivating the four gatekeepers
method_summary: Cultivating peace, inquiry, contentment and the company of the holy — all four, or at least one with full effort, since the others follow.

name: Weakening latent tendencies
method_summary: First replacing dark, object-bound tendencies with pure ones such as friendliness, then giving up all tendencies and even the desire for liberation.

name: Bhuśuṇḍa's contemplation of the breath
method_summary: Continuous contemplation of the natural movement of prāṇa and apāna from and to the heart, attending to the points where each subsides and resting in the Self in the pauses between them.
notes: Summary only; no counts or durations are recorded. The YV presents it as akin to contemplation of the Self, not as forced retention.

name: Stilling mind through the breath (Yoga Vāsiṣṭha)
method_summary: Because the vibration of prāṇa is one seed of the mind, yogins calm the mind by restraining the breath through prāṇāyāma, meditation and skilful methods; the other seed, vāsanā, must also be given up.

warnings.text: The Yoga Vāsiṣṭha holds that breath-stilling alone is insufficient without giving up vāsanās and gaining knowledge (U06 summary of 5.92).

name: Renunciation of everything (sarva-tyāga)
method_summary: True renunciation is the giving up of the mind itself, the root of all; outer renunciation of kingdom or belongings does not suffice while the notion 'I renounce' remains.

name: Resting as the witness (Aṣṭāvakra Gītā)
method_summary: Knowing oneself as the witness of the elements, body and mind, separating from the body and resting in consciousness, one is free now.

warnings.text: The practice of samādhi itself is called bondage from the absolute standpoint (1.15).

name: The four dissolutions (Aṣṭāvakra Gītā)
method_summary: Recognizing 'I am like space, the world a pot', 'I am the ocean, the world its waves', 'I am the shell, the world the imagined silver', 'I am in all beings and they in me' — after which nothing is to be renounced, accepted or dissolved.

name: Forgetting everything (Aṣṭāvakra Gītā)
method_summary: Abiding in oneself comes not from studying many scriptures but from forgetting everything.

name: Dissolving the syllables of Oṃ into the Self (Rāma Gītā)
method_summary: Before samādhi, contemplating the world as Oṃ; dissolving A (the waking viśva) into U, U (the dreaming taijasa) into M, and M (the sleeping prājña) into the Self, dense consciousness: 'I am the supreme Brahman'.

name: Understanding the great saying
method_summary: Understanding 'that thou art' by first grasping the words' meanings and then, by partial implication, the consciousness common to 'that' and 'thou', with faith and the teacher's grace.

name: The nine means of devotion (Adhyātma Rāmāyaṇa)
method_summary: Practising the nine means taught to Śabarī, beginning with holy company and ending with inquiry into the Lord's nature.

name: Ekādaśī fast
method_summary: Fasting on the eleventh lunar day, named among the causes of devotion to Rāma.
notes: U06 contributes only this source; details belong to the Purāṇa units.

name: Service of the teacher
method_summary: Serving and worshipping the teacher as the Lord in body, speech and mind; in the Guru Gītā the guru's satisfaction fulfils all practices.

name: Recitation of the Guru Gītā
method_summary: Reciting or chanting the Guru Gītā, prescribed in the text for success, protection and liberation at death; in recent times chanted daily in Muktananda's ashrams.

warnings.text: Not to be taught to the faithless, the deceiver or the hypocrite.

name: Meditation on the guru's form
method_summary: Meditating on the guru's form, the root of meditation, often visualized in the lotus of the head at dawn (Devī Gītā 7.40.1).

name: Kuṇḍalinī yoga of the Devī Gītā
method_summary: Summary only: after the eight limbs, the Goddess describes breath control, the channels and six centres, and the rousing of kuṇḍalinī from the root centre to union with the supreme at the crown; procedures, counts and retentions are not recorded here.

warnings.text: The Devī Gītā places this yoga after the yamas and niyamas and within devotion to the Goddess; the text is to be taught only to the qualified.

prerequisites: the ten yamas and ten niyamas

name: The ten yamas and ten niyamas (Devī Gītā)
method_summary: Practising the ten restraints and ten observances listed by the Goddess as the first limbs of yoga.

name: Internal worship (antaryāga)
method_summary: Worship of the Goddess performed inwardly, held higher than external worship in the Devī Gītā's close.
notes: U06 contribution to a shared practice id.

name: Purification of the elements (bhūta-śuddhi)
method_summary: Named in the Devī Gītā as a preliminary of daily worship (procedure not described here).
notes: U06 contribution to a shared practice id.

name: Placing letters and syllables on the body (nyāsa)
method_summary: In the Devī Gītā's daily worship: placing the letters (mātṛkā-nyāsa) and the syllable hrīṃ (hṛllekhā) in the body.
notes: U06 contribution to a shared practice id.

name: Pilgrimage (tīrthāṭana)
method_summary: Visiting sacred places: the Goddess's seats listed in the Devī Gītā, and pilgrimage among the Uddhava Gītā's niyamas; the Avadhūta Gītā's apology notes that pilgrimage presupposes a limit to the all-pervading.

name: Pāśupata yoga of the Īśvara Gītā
method_summary: Taking ash from the sacred fire and smearing all the limbs while reciting the 'agnir iti' mantras, then meditating on Īśāna, the supreme light, within; for celibate twice-born devotees.

name: The Virajā initiation (Śiva Gītā)
method_summary: An initiation with sacred ash and the Virajā mantras, taking the Pāśupata vow, before worship of Śiva.

name: Negation 'not this, not this'
method_summary: In the Rāma Gītā: negating the whole world by 'not this', tasting the consciousness in the heart and setting the world aside like the rind of a fruit whose juice is drunk.
notes: U06 contribution to a shared practice id (principal source: Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad).
